title: Organ flue pipe
reference_instrument: a different pipe, for family likeness and with no count: a 16 ft Principal at St. Jakobus, Ilmenau (MusicSphere Part 3, key B5, Mic 2, CC BY 4.0)
summary: One note, B4, on one measured tin flue pipe, beside a recording of a different pipe, so nothing is graded. It speaks the right mode, but it is far too clean, still hollow and slow to speak, and before it settles it plays a tone the real pipe doesn't have. The pipe comes from Castellengo's 2004 measurements and is blown at its measured 360 Pa through the paper's short attack. The jet isn't this pipe's own: its spreading law is a trial from Fletcher's 1976 E4 pipe, its 0.666 mm labium offset is carried from the same pipe, and the limit on its swing is his envelope with timing of our own. It holds 488.7 Hz, +49 c against the pipe's measured first resonance, most of that the passive network's own on one reading of the paper's length.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop on the generic flue network route (music_render wind): a jet driven by the foot pressure acting on a connected duct network, the route the recorder, tin whistle and pan pipes use, with no organ-shaped code
The measured pipe (Castellengo, ISMA 2004): 27 mm bore, 308.5 mm from mouth centre to open end, a mouth 21 mm wide with a 7 mm cut-up, and a 0.25 mm flue
The measured wind: 360 Pa, reached by the paper's short attack (125 Pa at 9 ms, 360 Pa at 45 ms)
The mouth's acoustic mass from its own 3-D wall cut, and radiation from the mouth and open end
Dry room air at 20 C, fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the bore

A forced Bickley jet, spreading by Fletcher 1976's organ-flue Pitot law. That's a trial here: it was measured on an E4 pipe with flues of 0.25 to 1.0 mm, so this flue is in range, but it isn't this pipe

A labium offset of 0.666 mm (2.66 flue heights). It isn't a measurement of this pipe: it carries Fletcher's voicing b0 of about -0.4, printed for his perspex E4 pipe, through his jet width at this cut-up
A limit on how far the jet can swing: Fletcher 1976's envelope, with no coefficient to set. The way it's applied in time is ours: the gain changes only when the jet changes sign
The first mode: it speaks 488.7 Hz from about 0.12 s on
physics_missing: A recording of this pipe: the clip is a 16 ft Principal at St. Jakobus, Ilmenau, key B5, sounding 482.85 Hz. Different pipe, so it's family likeness only with no count, and nothing about it went into the card. The 21.0 c between them isn't a fault

Noise: the harmonics-to-noise gap to the recording is 55.7 dB. The card has no jet noise: that row's gate opens at a flue Reynolds number of 700, and this flue runs near 400. The real pipe's floor may also come from its blower, valve or room
Even harmonics: odd stand +3.3 dB over even, against -10.9 dB in the recording. H2 is still about 15 dB under even the two lower microphones on the real pipe, and it leans on the borrowed offset
Prompt speech: the attack takes 187.2 ms, 10 to 90 %, against 16.6 ms. The card's ramp reaches 360 Pa at 45 ms, so it isn't the ramp, and the cause is unexplained
The right first sound: a tone near 1530 Hz, the pipe's third mode, leads from 20 to 100 ms. The recording opens on its own second harmonic at 966 Hz
The high harmonics: H5 to H11 sit 3 to 35 dB under the recording, all above 2 kHz, where the compact receiver on this route isn't valid, so it may not all be the jet
A jet at a real pipe's swing: its swing is still 13 flue heights, where de la Cuadra 2005 records a free jet at 3.3 to 3.95

Pitch: about 40 c of the +49 c is the passive network's own 486 Hz with the length read from the languid. The paper doesn't say where its 312 mm is measured from, and the upper-lip reading gives 476 Hz. On the card without the swing limit, the pitch also moved with a numerical setting

This pipe's own voicing, and what the paper doesn't state: the wall thickness, the point the length is measured from, the upper lip, the flattened mouth, the flue's depth, the languid, the foot, the toe hole and the room
Mouth tones, chiff and wind noise of the attack. The route has no hydrodynamic feedback from the labium to the flue and no resolved jet, so it can't make edge tones
